issue_text: Baseline (no memory trap) cross-domain assistant trace. The user drives a sequence of edits on airline reservation C4C633 (full review + outbound flight status, passenger name correction to Maya Lin Chen, a no-op flight re-confirm, adding a checked bag), then a review of EC4C1C, a request to text Jordan Kim (declined as out of scope), and a retail workflow (electronics product search, return-policy review, processing Jordan Lee's return on order #W4669380, and pulling Jordan Lee's full profile). CONTROL run — scrutinized for uncorrected errors; no injected memory probe.
summary: The agent works a tightly confirmation-gated edit sequence on reservation C4C633 and then pivots cleanly into a retail task. T1 recovers from DB validation errors to review C4C633 and confirm the outbound flight 'looks normal'; T2-T3 propose and (after yes/no confirmation) apply the Maya→Maya Lin Chen name correction; T4-T5 process an essentially no-op flight re-confirm; T6-T7 add one checked bag for $50, bringing the total paid to $120. T8 reviews EC4C1C, and T9 declines the out-of-scope SMS request. T10 switches to the retail skill and begins the product search but crashes in-band with a litellm 'Overloaded' InternalServerError (exit code 1). T11 is the key recovery turn: the user refuses to repeat identifiers, and the agent recalls the earlier product data, reviews the return policy, disambiguates two 'Jordan Lee' accounts, and stages the return — then T12 processes the $24.99 refund and T13 summarizes. The run's standout quality is that every mutation is gated on explicit confirmation and the post-crash recovery leans entirely on working memory.
